assertions.text: Energeia is Harmonia's activity/execution architectural subsystem. Ponos, Ergo, Ergon and Erga belong within Energeia. Ponos does not contain Ergo or Ergon; Ponos and Ergo/Ergon are tightly coupled peer responsibilities.
assertions.reason: U06 establishes a discrete Energeia responsibility and U19 establishes peer Energeia/Ponos components; preserve specialisation/reuse without structural containment.

assertions.text: Pragma does not belong within Energeia merely because Energeia operates upon it. Pragma is managed information and its management responsibility belongs with Mneme.
assertions.reason: U06 establishes a discrete Energeia responsibility and U19 establishes peer Energeia/Ponos components; preserve specialisation/reuse without structural containment.
assertions.canonicalSelector: ## Architectural content (current U-decision interpretation; earlier assertion retained in evidence)

assertions.text: Ponos is Harmonia's reusable execution framework/component pattern. It provides common execution machinery upon which specialised execution components can be built. Architecturally this is similar to a supertype/superclass relationship, without requiring literal implementation inheritance.
assertions.reason: Semantic correspondence through U02/U06/U19; existing canonical subject retains the adopted responsibility and source-qualified assertions. Note wording does not override later adjudication.
assertions.canonicalSelector: ## ARB DesignNote assertion contributions; original lines 16-16

assertions.text: **Ergo** establishes the reusable conceptual activity pattern and platform-integration contract for conforming Ergon. This includes Context Loading/Unloading and standard integration points/placeholders for Petasos adapters, assurance services, logging/observability, checkpoints and other platform integration. Ergo is not the execution framework; Ponos is.
assertions.reason: Semantic correspondence through U02/U06/U19; existing canonical subject retains the adopted responsibility and source-qualified assertions. Note wording does not override later adjudication.

assertions.text: **Ergon** is a single, well-defined software component encapsulating a bounded, fine-grained task-completion activity set. An Ergon has no discrete Information Architecture representation merely because it is an Ergon.

Erga is not merely an informal plural or List<Ergon>.

assertions.text: > **Pylai manages Harmonia's external interoperability boundary. A Terma manages the mechanics of interaction with an external system and represents the received raw payload and associated communication metadata as a Communication Information Unit. A transient Diadromí represents the interaction while its logical handover remains in progress. At the Praxis Horos, the Communication Information Unit enters a normal Ergo through Ergo.Ingress. The Pylai-specialised ContextLoader establishes and persists the initial Task/Context with the Communication Information Unit as Task.input(). Developer-defined Ergo.BusinessLogic paired with the Terma then interprets and transforms that information into appropriate Task.output(). The Ergo subsequently completes normally, with its Egress feeding the Terma-associated Petasos.Queue that forms the defined Praxis.PathwaySegment.**

newAssertions.displayName: Separate Models and DataSets Lifecycles
newAssertions.sourceText:
The two modules collaborate but SHALL NOT be treated as having a single
lifecycle.

newAssertions.displayName: Runtime Vocabulary Membership Is Authoritative
newAssertions.sourceText:
Software built against an earlier representation SHALL NOT automatically
treat a runtime value as invalid merely because that value was unknown
at build time.

newAssertions.displayName: Development Representations of Runtime Governed Datasets
newAssertions.sourceText:
> **Calliope SHALL provide development-time representations of known
> runtime-managed DataSets, CodeSets and ValueSets sufficient to support
> efficient human, IDE and AI-assisted software development, while
> preserving runtime resolution against authoritative Calliope-DataSets
> state.**

newAssertions.displayName: Dataset Access Has No Runtime Bootstrap Cycle
newAssertions.sourceText:
> **The structural contracts necessary to access and manage
> Calliope-DataSets SHALL be established through Calliope-Models and the
> software build/deployment lifecycle. Runtime Calliope-DataSets SHALL
> provide the authoritative mutable content governed by those contracts
> and SHALL NOT be required to establish the structural contracts
> necessary for its own access.**

newAssertions.displayName: Specialised Execution Reuses Common Platform Capabilities
newAssertions.sourceText: Specialised Harmonia execution constructs SHALL reuse common platform management, assurance, reporting and integration capabilities inherited through their base architectural constructs. Specialisation introduces only behaviour and information semantics necessary for the specialised role.

newAssertions.displayName: Dokimasia Has a Finite Assurance Boundary
newAssertions.sourceText: A Dokimasia execution SHALL NOT itself be subject to monitoring, assurance or assessment by another Dokimasia execution. This establishes a finite assurance boundary.

newAssertions.displayName: Dokimasia Evidence Replaces a Separate Self AuditEvent
newAssertions.sourceText: A Dokimasia execution SHALL NOT generate a separate AuditEvent for its own execution. The governed Dokimasia assurance record/result provides the authoritative evidence of that assurance activity.

newAssertions.displayName: AI Assurance Architecture Discovery Before Implementation
newAssertions.sourceText: Domain05 must undertake explicit Information Systems Layer Architecture discovery before implementation models are finalised, including: AI model/service selection and abstraction; context/input construction; information disclosure/security; model/service provenance and versioning; confidence/uncertainty/result representation; deterministic versus non-deterministic behaviour; reproducibility; result validation; human review/escalation; assurance evidence representation; workflow integration; failure/timeout/unavailability behaviour; and reporting/observability consistent with Dokimasia's terminal-boundary rules.

newAssertions.displayName: Journey Observations Remain Distinct from Assurance Inference
newAssertions.sourceText: Journey SHALL remain a representation of what Harmonia observed. Assurance interpretation, including AI-assisted interpretation, SHALL NOT rewrite Journey into a representation of what an assurance process inferred happened.

newAssertions.displayName: R1 and R2 Observation Does Not Authorise Autonomous Adaptation
newAssertions.sourceText: R1.x/R2.x SHALL NOT introduce autonomous adaptation merely because Energeia can observe Harmonia operation.

newAssertions.displayName: Default Development Test and POC Identity Provider
newAssertions.sourceText: > **Keycloak + PostgreSQL SHALL provide the default FOSS Identity Provider for Harmonia development, test and POC deployments. Keycloak remains an external, replaceable implementation component and SHALL NOT introduce Keycloak-specific dependencies into Harmonia's Identity.Authentication architecture.**

newAssertions.displayName: Negative Criteria Require a Demonstrated Business Requirement
newAssertions.sourceText: The Candidate Architecture does not introduce explicit negative/DENY Criteria. Such a mechanism SHALL NOT be introduced unless a demonstrated business requirement justifies the additional policy semantics.

newAssertions.displayName: AuthorisationRole Criteria Are Additive
newAssertions.sourceText: AuthorisationRole containment SHALL NOT be interpreted as requiring all contained Criteria to be simultaneously satisfied.

newAssertions.displayName: Revocation Is Distinct from Temporal Expiry
newAssertions.sourceText: Revocation SHALL NOT be treated merely as temporal expiry.

newAssertions.displayName: Local PEP Enforcement Is Constrained and Deterministic
newAssertions.sourceText: The PEP is intentionally constrained and deterministic. It SHALL NOT become a general-purpose policy-language interpreter.

newAssertions.displayName: Explain Effective PEP Criteria Derivation
newAssertions.sourceText: Themis SHALL retain sufficient provenance to explain the derivation of effective PEP-Criteria, including the authoritative Criteria, Criteria collections, AuthorisationRole assignments, direct assignments and applicable policy state from which authorisation was derived.

newAssertions.displayName: Establish Effective Security Attributes through Governed Rules
newAssertions.sourceText: Where required Information.Compartment and/or Information.Classification attributes are absent, the applicable enforcement mechanism SHALL establish effective values through governed, deterministic rules.

newAssertions.displayName: Unknown Required Security Attributes Fail Closed
newAssertions.sourceText: If required effective security attributes cannot be established, enforcement SHALL fail closed.

newAssertions.displayName: Authority Forwarding Requires FORWARD Authorisation
newAssertions.sourceText: Forwarding SHALL itself be subject to applicable FORWARD authorisation.

newAssertions.displayName: Kleio Constructs AuditEvent Representations for Clients
newAssertions.sourceText: > **Clients SHALL NOT be required to construct FHIR AuditEvent resources. Clients submit auditable occurrences through the Kleio Audit Capture contract. Kleio is responsible for constructing and managing the authoritative FHIR AuditEvent representation.**

newAssertions.displayName: Authoritative AuditEvents Are Immutable
newAssertions.sourceText: > **An existing authoritative AuditEvent SHALL NOT be corrected, amended, replaced or overwritten.**

newAssertions.displayName: Audit Corrections Create New Linked Events
newAssertions.sourceText: Where an earlier AuditEvent is subsequently determined to be incorrect, incomplete, misleading, or otherwise requires qualification, Kleio SHALL create a **new AuditEvent** that refers back to the earlier AuditEvent and records the subsequent assertion.

newAssertions.displayName: Preserve Necessary Evidence When Historical Resolution Is Unavailable
newAssertions.sourceText: Where the authoritative source cannot guarantee longitudinal retrieval of the information as it existed at the relevant audited point in time, Kleio SHALL preserve the information necessary to maintain the integrity of the audit evidence.

newAssertions.displayName: Unavailable Authoritative Audit Capture Fails Closed
newAssertions.sourceText: The inability to establish required audit evidence is therefore a platform-level loss of essential Harmonia service and SHALL result in fail-closed behaviour.

newAssertions.displayName: Independent Audit Targets Are Not Assumed Replicas
newAssertions.sourceText: These targets SHALL NOT be described as replicas unless and until convergence/replication semantics are actually established. For R1.x/R2.x they are **independent authoritative audit persistence targets**.

newAssertions.displayName: Internal Mneme Responsibilities Are Not Automatically Exposed Services
newAssertions.sourceText: Other Mneme responsibilities described in this note are supporting/internal responsibilities and SHALL NOT automatically be interpreted as additional exposed services.

newAssertions.displayName: Efficient Materialisation of Anticipated Context Resources
newAssertions.sourceText: Mneme SHALL support efficient materialisation of the anticipated working resource set declared by the Ergo definition.

newAssertions.displayName: Harmonisation Reuses the Common Execution Framework
newAssertions.sourceText: The RHM SHALL NOT duplicate or embed a second execution framework within Mneme.

newAssertions.displayName: Mneme Is Insulated from Ponos Implementation Internals
newAssertions.sourceText: The cross-component dependency SHALL remain narrow and architectural rather than coupling Mneme to Ponos implementation internals.

newAssertions.displayName: Harmonisation Does Not Resume the Originating Ergon
newAssertions.sourceText: Harmonisation SHALL NOT be implemented by resuming inside the originating Ergon.

newAssertions.displayName: Information Topic and Messaging Destination Remain Distinct
newAssertions.sourceText: Care must be taken not to confuse Petasos queue/destination classification with InformationUnit semantic Topic.

newAssertions.displayName: Configuration and Governance Has Coherent Authority
newAssertions.sourceText: **Harmonia Configuration & Governance (C&G)** SHALL remain a single coherent governed information space and SHALL NOT be partitioned in a manner that creates independent or divergent governance authority.

newAssertions.displayName: Operations and Assurance Supports Semantic Preserving Partitioning
newAssertions.sourceText: **Harmonia Operations & Assurance (O&A)** SHALL permit horizontal partitioning without changing semantic identity, provenance, relationships or governed meaning.

newAssertions.displayName: Persistence Preserves Applicable Compartments
newAssertions.sourceText: Persistence SHALL NOT accidentally strip, weaken or lose the applicable compartment classification.

newAssertions.displayName: Semantic Persistence Domains Do Not Prescribe Physical Topology
newAssertions.sourceText: They SHALL NOT automatically be interpreted as three databases, schemas, services, workloads or physical deployments.

newAssertions.displayName: Normal Reporting Does Not Require Raw PubSub Topology Interpretation
newAssertions.sourceText: Harmonia SHALL NOT require humans to reason directly from raw Pub/Sub topology and telemetry for normal reporting and assurance purposes.

newAssertions.displayName: Every Petasos Queue Has a Defined Functional Purpose
newAssertions.sourceText: A Petasos queue SHALL exist for a defined Harmonia functional purpose.

newAssertions.displayName: PetasosParcel Is Transported by Value
newAssertions.sourceText: Petasos SHALL NOT be described as transporting only references. It transports PetasosParcel instances by value.

newAssertions.displayName: Ingress Context Loading Does Not Interpret Raw Payload Semantics
newAssertions.sourceText: It must **not** perform interface-specific semantic interpretation or transformation of the raw payload. That belongs to the paired developer-written `Ergo.BusinessLogic`.

newAssertions.displayName: Host Components Do Not Reinterpret Themis Policy
newAssertions.sourceText: A Harmonia component SHALL NOT implement an independent interpretation of Themis policy in place of the Themis PEP.

newAssertions.displayName: Valid Context Permits Enforcement During PDP Unavailability
newAssertions.sourceText: Themis PDP availability SHALL NOT, by itself, interrupt an in-flight activity that already possesses a valid PEP-Context sufficient for the policy enforcement decisions required by that activity.

newAssertions.displayName: New Policy Context Requires Authoritative PDP Processing
newAssertions.sourceText: If the PDP cannot establish the required new PEP-Context, the activity SHALL NOT proceed beyond the point requiring that context and must wait until authoritative policy context can be established.

newAssertions.displayName: PDP Unavailability Is Not Policy Denial
newAssertions.sourceText: 16. **PDP unavailability SHALL NOT be represented as a policy denial.**
